$schema: Entries are listed newest-first. Each entry: { date: YYYY-MM-DD, type, summary, details?, files? }. Types: added | changed | fixed | removed | docs | chore.

entries.summary: AI skills now ship with the design system
details: Services automatically receive updated AI agent instructions when they update the design system. No manual sync needed.

entries.summary: AI-built services now match wireframes more faithfully and use the right card for KPIs
details: AI agents building services from the starter template now preserve multi-column wireframe layouts at desktop widths instead of folding them into a single column
The dedicated KPI card is now the default for any "number + label + icon" tile; the generic card is reserved for grouping other content
Captured a known design-system styling glitch with its workaround, with auto-tracking so the workaround comes off as soon as the next release fixes it

entries.summary: Services now render the correct light-mode colors and sidebar styling without extra setup
details: Service teams using the design system were seeing washed-out backgrounds in light mode and a missing sidebar surface — a piece the published bundle wasn't exposing
Bumping @dpds-gov/design-system to 0.1.2 in a service repo fixes it; Dependabot will offer the bump automatically on the next weekly run

entries.summary: Installation guide added to the docs
details: A new Installation page under Getting Started walks teams through generating their access token, cloning a fresh service from the template, setting it up locally, and using the AI-assisted workflow to build their first service
Includes a troubleshooting table for the most common setup gotchas — expired tokens, wrong repo owner, missing CI secret, light-mode colours

entries.summary: Services no longer need to install extra translation libraries to use the design system
details: Earlier today's first release quietly required every team to install two extra translation libraries just so components flipped correctly between English and Arabic
This follow-up reads the page direction directly from the page itself — no extra libraries required
Teams that already use translation libraries for their own copy keep working unchanged

entries.summary: Design system released — service teams can now use it in their own projects
details: First public release of the design system, available to any team building a Dubai Police service
A starter template is now live — teams click 'Use this template' on GitHub to spin up a brand-new service and have it running in about ten minutes

Includes a fully working sample dashboard showing the standard page header, a grid of chart and KPI cards, and a paginated requests table — the common building blocks every service is expected to compose from

entries.summary: Example layouts across the docs site are now consistent two-column
details: Every page that shows example components now uses the same two-column side-by-side layout, even on narrow screens, so examples are easier to compare at a glance
Replaced one-off input-with-icon arrangements across the site with the standard grouped-input pattern, so search fields, prefixed inputs, and inline buttons all look and behave the same everywhere
Tightened a few spacing and motion details that surfaced along the way

entries.summary: Fixed broken Label links in seven Form & Input pages
details: Clicking 'Label' in the Related section of seven form pages was sending users to a placeholder 'Coming Soon' screen — now it opens the real Label page
Removed the unused placeholder screen so it can't be reached by accident anymore

entries.summary: Browser tab icon updated to the Dubai Police Logo
details: Replaces the generic purple icon that came with the starter template
Adjusted so it stays crisp at any browser tab size

entries.summary: Cleaner sidebar with collapsible groups, plus a new footer on every page
details: Each sidebar group (Getting Started, Foundations, Form & Input, and so on) can now be collapsed or expanded. Getting Started opens by default
Added a footer on every page showing the Dubai Police Design System 2.0 name and copyright line. The thin line above the footer runs all the way across the screen for visual consistency
The thin divider above the 'Related components' section on every component page is now tighter, and it's now applied automatically across all pages instead of being added one at a time
The sidebar's open/close button looks lighter, matching the page style better

entries.summary: New Getting Started section with Introduction, Project Structure, Theming, and Dark Mode pages
details: Built four new documentation pages: Introduction, Project Structure, Theming, and Dark Mode
Added a new theme switcher in the header — choose Light, Dark, or 'Match my system' with a smooth sun-to-moon animation
Cleaned up an older duplicate Typography page so there's only one (under Foundations)
Theming page shows the real colors used in light and dark mode side by side, so designers and developers can compare exact tones at a glance
The whole product is now called Dubai Police Design System 2.0 (DPDS 2.0). Older draft names have been removed throughout
Example branding swapped from a placeholder brand to DPDS, and example email addresses now use @dubaipolice.gov.ae

entries.summary: Nine new layout-related pages and seven new building blocks
details: Added pages for: Aspect Ratio, Separator, Container, Collapsible, Scroll Area, Grid, Stack, Accordion, Resizable

Seven new building blocks teams can use: Aspect Ratio (keeps image proportions), Container (centered content with a max width), Collapsible (show/hide sections), Scroll Area (custom scrollbars), Grid (responsive layouts), Stack (vertical or horizontal stacks with optional dividers), Resizable (drag-to-resize panels)
The original plan listed only three of these — we discovered four more were also missing and built them too
All pages verified to load successfully

entries.summary: Six new Feedback & Overlay pages, plus updated Alert styles
details: Added pages for: Spinner, Progress, Alert, Popover, Hover Card, and Drawer/Sheet
Two new building blocks: Spinner (loading indicator) and Hover Card (preview-on-hover popover)
Alerts can now appear in four tones — info, success, warning, and error — matching how the rest of the system uses color
Clarified the difference between Drawer (mobile, drag-to-dismiss) and Sheet (desktop side panels) on a shared documentation page

entries.summary: Cleaned up leftover old code and translated more hardcoded text
details: Removed unused leftover code from an older shared page that's no longer needed by Badges, Breadcrumb, Stepper, or Menu — each of those now has its own dedicated page
Took five strings on the Colors page and three on the Iconography page out of hardcoded English and into the translation system, so they're ready for Arabic and other languages
Decided to keep Progress Tracker and Stepper as two separate building blocks because they're used differently — the older plan to merge them won't work
Flagged that table headers across the eight Foundation pages still need translating — that's a separate follow-up task

entries.summary: New Data Table page with nine real-world examples
details: Covers everything teams typically need: searching, sorting, filtering by status, selecting rows, row actions, an Add button, empty state, and loading state
Uses twelve realistic example tickets across different statuses, priorities, and assignees so teams can see how a real CRM table would look

entries.summary: Ten new pages for Data Display and Navigation
details: Added pages for: Badge, Avatar, Skeleton (loading shape), Breadcrumb, Pagination, Stepper, Command palette, Menu, Context Menu (right-click menu), and Navbar
Four new building blocks for teams to use: Pagination, Command palette, Context Menu, and Navbar
Renamed the older Navigation Menu file for clarity

entries.summary: Four new Form & Input pages, including a Combobox
details: Added Label, Switch, Slider, and Combobox pages
Combobox is a new control that combines a dropdown with a search-and-filter field — supports single or multi-select, grouping, custom entry, and loading from a server
Switch and Slider pages each show seven real-world examples (notification settings list, range with two thumbs, vertical orientation, and more)
All ten Form & Input pages now point to real documentation — no more 'Coming Soon' placeholders

entries.summary: Five brand-new components: Tag, Banner, Empty State, List, and Stat Tile
details: Tag — colored labels with selected and removable variants, six colors, two sizes. Acts as a clickable button when needed
Banner — full-width notice at the top of a page (info, success, warning, error) with an optional action button and dismiss control
Empty State — friendly empty-space message for when there's nothing to show (no results, no data, error, no permission)
List — flexible rows for items with a leading icon, title, description, and trailing action. Comes in dense and comfortable spacing, with optional dividers
Stat Tile — KPI summary card with a label, big value, up/down change indicator, icon, and a small inline chart line

entries.summary: Each component page now lists the design tokens it uses
details: Every component page (Button, Input, Select, Card, Tabs, Tooltip, Toast, Dialog, Sidebar, Form, Table, Textarea, Checkbox, Radio, Datepicker, Input OTP, File Upload) now ends with a footer naming the foundations the component depends on — and links straight to each foundation page
Helps teams see at a glance that, for example, Tooltips use Colors, Radius, Spacing, Typography, Elevation, and Motion

entries.summary: New Accessibility page with rules, checklist, and external resources
details: Covers five core topics: Keyboard, Screen reader (ARIA), Color contrast, Motion, and Touch targets
Eight-item pre-merge checklist for teams to run through before shipping any feature
Curated external resources: WCAG, ARIA, axe DevTools, WebAIM, Inclusive Components
All eight foundation pages (Colors, Typography, Spacing, Radius, Motion, Elevation, Iconography, Accessibility) are now complete — no more 'Coming Soon' placeholders

entries.summary: Added animated icons section to the Iconography page
details: New section showing six animated icons — tickets, completed request, and four general motion icons
Each animated icon plays automatically. A link points to the full gallery of 52 icons for browsing

entries.summary: New Iconography page with live icon library, sizes, and usage rules
details: Sample of eight commonly used icons (Settings, Bell, Mail, Calendar, Search, Download, Check, Alert)
Size guide: 16px, 20px, 24px, 32px — each shown with a live preview and typical uses
Line-thickness guide and color examples
Common patterns: icon-only button, icon + text, decorative icon, and leading icon in input field
Six accessibility and usage rules to follow when adding icons

entries.summary: New Elevation page with shadow styles and layering rules
details: Added four named shadow styles for common surfaces (card, popover, modal, toast)
Added a nine-level layering system so cards, popovers, modals, tooltips, and more always stack in the right order — no more guessing layer numbers
Page shows the named shadows next to the full Tailwind shadow scale and explains when to use each

entries.summary: New Motion page with duration and easing options
details: Defines a five-step duration scale (instant → slower) and a small set of easing curves teams can use
Hover-to-play demos let teams see exactly how each duration and easing feels
Reduced-motion section reminds teams to respect a user's 'reduce motion' setting — and includes ready-to-copy code for apps to add
Usage rules: when small things should be fast, when bigger things should be slow, what easing to use for entry vs exit, and more

entries.summary: New Border Radius page showing the corner-rounding scale
details: Nine corner-rounding values (none → very rounded → fully rounded) shown as live shape samples
Sample card mixes different corner styles (input, button, container, avatar) to show how they nest visually
Usage rules cover consistency, outer-bigger-than-inner nesting, when to use 'fully rounded', and avoiding random values

entries.summary: New Spacing & Layout page with the spacing scale and layout tips
details: 17-step spacing scale from 0 to 128px shown as live width bars
Reference for container widths (prose width through extra-large)
Cheat-sheet of common spacing utilities (padding, margin, gap, max width)
Usage rules: stick to the scale, prefer gap over manual spacing, and support right-to-left languages

entries.summary: New Typography page with fonts, sizes, and writing rules
details: Two fonts shown with every available weight: Dubai (sans-serif) and Bukra (monospace)
Nine-step type scale from Display headlines down to small Caption labels — each shown at actual size with proper line height
Usage rules cover line length, line spacing, using font weight to show hierarchy, and when monospace is appropriate

entries.summary: New Colors page with the full palette and color tokens
details: Colors page shows about 29 named colors (surface, brand, status, border, sidebar) with light and dark values side by side
Color contrast labels (AAA, AA, AA Large) on each text color so teams can see at a glance which combinations are accessible
Full palette shown in a familiar tailwindcss.com style — 12 shades for each of the 16 color scales (gray, slate, sage, brand greens, blues, status reds and yellows and greens, and more)
Click any color to copy its variable name, shift-click to copy the Tailwind class
Includes an opacity demo and a sample notification card to show colors in real use

entries.summary: New File Upload page (single and multi-file)
details: Replaces the older shared documentation
Covers both single-file and multi-file uploaders on one page
Ten total examples: five for single-file (default, file-type filter, label, change handler, images only) and five for multi-file (default, max count, file-type filter, change handler, label)

entries.summary: New One-Time Password (OTP) input page
details: Replaces the 'Coming Soon' placeholder
Eight examples: default, with a separator between digit groups, digits-only, four-digit short code, controlled value, auto-submit when complete, error state, and disabled
Live demos for controlled value and auto-submit on completion

entries.summary: New Datepicker page
details: Replaces the older shared documentation
Shows the recommended pattern (popover + calendar) instead of a single all-in-one control
Eight examples: single date, date range (two months side by side), multiple dates, min/max date limits, inline picker, default month, year/month dropdown navigation, and with a label

entries.summary: New Radio page
details: Replaces the older shared documentation
Eight examples covering default value, controlled value, descriptions, horizontal layout, disabling the whole group or just one option, and required field
Live demo for controlled selection (delivery method picker)

entries.summary: New Checkbox page
details: Replaces the older shared documentation
Nine examples including indeterminate state, select-all parent-and-child pattern, and multi-select groups
Live demos for indeterminate cycling and parent-child selection

entries.summary: New Textarea page
details: Replaces the older shared documentation
Follows the standard layout: preview, install, usage, examples, props, accessibility, related
Examples cover auto-resize, character counter, fixed height, error state, disabled, and read-only

entries.summary: Changelog entries now use the standard card style
details: Updated visual style — the gradient border, soft background, and subtle dark-mode shadow now match the rest of the docs

entries.summary: New Changelog page and automated update workflow
details: New /docs/changelog page that reads from a data file
Automated reminder so user-visible changes get logged when work is finished
Adds a skill that handles the changelog update procedure

entries.summary: Ten new dedicated pages — one per component
details: New dedicated pages for: Input, Select, Card, Tabs, Tooltip, Toast, Dialog, Sidebar, Form, and Table
Each page follows the standard layout: preview, install, usage, examples, props, accessibility, related
Per-page migration notes kept in the internal log
